newsitem.title: CHINA: FORECAST-China 1997 oil output seen up 4.2-5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-China 1997 oil output seen up 4.2-5.5 pct.

text.p: China is expected to produce 165-167 million tonnes of crude oil this year, up 4.2-5.5 percent from last year, officials and state media said on Tuesday.

China has not announced an actual figure for total crude oil production for 1996 though it had previously estimated output at 155.3 million tonnes. The latest figures appeared to show 1996 output was above target.
Demand for crude oil was forecast at 175-177 million tonnes in 1997, up 4.8-6.0 percent from 1996, an official of the State Information Centre told Reuters.
Demand for refined oil products would exceed supply in 1997, the Economic Information Daily said.
Gasoline output was expected to be 35.12 million tonnes this year while consumption would be 35.5 million tonnes, it said.
Diesel output would be 47 million tonnes in 1997 while demand would hit 49.5 million tonnes.
Kerosene and fuel oil output were forecast at 5.5 million tonnes and 12.45 million tonnes with projected demand at 5.2 million and 12.60 million tonnes, respectively, it said.
The Economic Information Daily blamed lagging output on inadequate investment in the oil industry.
